findings.issue: op: "productVariants" is not a recognised Shopify Admin GraphQL operation. The spec requires every shopifySteps op to be resolved via the catalog tools; this name appears to have been composed from memory. The coding agent will attempt to call a non-existent operation and get a compile/runtime error, silently breaking the admin item-picker flow.
findings.fix: Run get_shopify_op on the correct op for fetching variant details by id — the standard Admin API approach is either the "nodes" query (accepts an array of variant GIDs) or "productVariant" (single id); resolve the exact op name and signature from the catalog tool before emitting, and update shopifySteps accordingly.

findings.issue: shopifySteps lists "discountAutomaticAppCreate" (step 0) and "discountAutomaticAppUpdate" (step 1) as an ordered sequential pipeline — the spec defines a multi-step list as one where "each step names what it produces and what the next step consumes." These two ops are conditional alternatives (create when no discount_external_id exists, update when one does), never both executed in sequence. Presenting them as a pipeline will mislead the coding agent into always calling both, which would create a new discount AND then attempt to update it, producing duplicate discounts on every bundle save.
findings.fix: Split sync-bundle-discount into two separate capabilities — "create-bundle-discount" (single step: discountAutomaticAppCreate) and "update-bundle-discount" (single step: discountAutomaticAppUpdate) — or document the branching intent in the capability description and list only one step per branch, letting the coding agent choose by the presence of discount_external_id.

findings.issue: Both the bundles.discount_value column and bundle_discount_tiers.discount_value column declare role: "ratio", but their purposes explicitly state they can hold "a flat amount depending on discount_kind" / "the discount fraction or amount granted at this tier". The spec defines ratio as "fractional values bounded between 0 and 1"; a flat monetary discount amount is unbounded and is a money role. Using ratio for money prevents the platform's money helper from applying correct minor-unit math on flat-amount discounts, and the column type the coding agent picks (e.g. REAL/DECIMAL vs. INTEGER cents) will be wrong for monetary values.
findings.fix: Either split discount_value into two columns — discount_ratio (role: ratio, nullable) and discount_amount (role: money, nullable) — with exactly one populated per discount_kind, or document that the column always stores a ratio (0–1) and flat amounts are stored in a separate column; update both tables and any capability that reads these columns.

findings.issue: get-bundle-for-edit (description: "Return a single bundle's full definition … for the admin edit form") and get-bundle-for-product (description: "Return the enabled bundle definition … for a given storefront product") both declare returnsList: true. The spec states returnsList must be set true when "the capability shows multiple records they can browse, sort, filter, or paginate" — both capabilities return a single bundle object (with nested item/tier lists). Setting returnsList: true incorrectly binds both capabilities to the paginate helper, which the coding agent will apply to the top-level bundle response rather than to the nested item/tier collections, breaking single-record fetch routes.
findings.fix: Set returnsList: false on both get-bundle-for-edit and get-bundle-for-product; remove "page cursor" from their dataNeeds; if the nested items/tiers lists need pagination, handle that in the contract's requestShape (cursor already declared there) without flagging the parent capability as a list.
